correctness.rationale: The span-subset identity is stated with all binomial normalizations: E1=25/3-(a1+a2)/3-a3, E2=25/3-b2/3-b3. Zero columns are dominated by coupling. Every rank-three four-vector configuration has a unique one-dimensional relation of support 2, 3, or 4; the proof reconstructs and bounds the counted recovery subsets in all three cases. A separate structural argument shows E2<4 forces E1>=4, completing the Pareto dominance proof. Four explicit rank-three witnesses attain pairwise-incomparable points in every field. Independent exact subset and Markov computations agree for all 119 binary and 1404 ternary projective multisets; experiments check small cases, not the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: Finite-length Pareto optimality of file-dedicated MDS codes is explicitly posed in the recent primary literature. This result settles its natural first-redundancy three-information-symbol case for every finite field and resolves the entire achievable efficient tradeoff, including two additional mixed frontier points and nonsystematic matrices. A relation-support proof supplies meaningful geometric structure rather than a single arbitrary small-field census.
